To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the addition of a limited amount of CNTs to TiO2 nanoparticles in DSCs leads to enhanced electron lifetime and reduced electron recombination.
the addition of a small amount of CNTs to the photoanodes leads to enhanced short circuit current density, electron lifetime, and overall photoconversion efficiencies of the DSCs.

CNTs can be added to TiO2 nanoparticles in a fast and effective way and that the resulting hybrid photoanodes lead to highly increased photoconversion efficiency in dye-sensitized cells, while no chemical treatments are needed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel, efficient and scalable procedure for the preparation and application of CNTs in DSCs, which can be easily extended to other photoelectrochemical cells.
the development of a simple and efficient method to produce hybrid photoanodes based on nanocrystals of TiO2 with a very low amount of CNTs.
the development of a simple, effective, and fast procedure to fabricate highly efficient hybrid CNTs–TiO2 photoanodes, which can be used for large-scale fabrication of DSCs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the first time, we demonstrate the possibility of using CNTs to improve DSC performance without the need to use chemical treatments.
CNTs are an effective additive to TiO2 in DSCs, which leads to enhanced short circuit current density, while open circuit photovoltages are reduced.
the addition of CNTs in TiO2 photoelectrodes is a promising strategy to improve the performances of DSCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the addition of a small amount of CNTs to the nanocrystallite TiO2 photoanode is an efficient way to increase the efficiency of DSCs, and that the effect of the CNTs on the TiO2 photoelectrode is mainly related to the electron lifetime.

the CNTs are able to increase electron lifetime, which leads to higher short circuit current density, and to a slight reduction of the open circuit photovoltages, which does not significantly affect the overall cell efficiency, as long as no TiCl4 post-treatment of photoanodes is used.

the addition of a limited amount of CNTs to a nanocrystallite TiO2 photoanode leads to an increase in the short circuit current density (Jsc) and in the overall efficiency (η) of the DSCs, without any significant reduction in the open circuit photovoltages (Voc).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the addition of CNTs to nanocrystallline TiO2 can be a very effective strategy for improving the efficiency of dye-sensitized cells without resorting to complex and expensive procedures.
the use of CNTs as additives to TiO2 in DSCs can be very advantageous, as it can significantly increase cell performance with no additional costs.
a small amount of CNTs is sufficient to significantly improve cell performances, which makes this approach suitable for large-scale production.
